title: Availability states on this device
blurb: Canonical Translator.availability() probe reading raw available, downloadable, downloading, and unavailable tokens for any language pair and navigator.languages without starting a download, alongside companion LanguageDetector availability.
question: Which raw Availability tokens does Translator.availability() report for supported, unsupported, and identity language pairs on this device, and what should a mobile UI do for each state?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153 headless (Linux), en->es and en->hi resolved "downloadable", en->kl resolved "unavailable", and LanguageDetector.availability() resolved "unavailable" with zero console errors. Chrome for Android 161 with an installed pack ("available") not verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 headless (Linux); not verified on Chrome for Android 161

friction.summary: Translator.availability() collapses unsupported pairs, identity pairs, permissions-policy denial, and TranslatorAPIAllowed=false into a single "unavailable" token, and may mask installed packs as "downloadable"
friction.repro: Compare Translator.availability() across en->kl, en->en, and a policy-denied iframe; all three return "unavailable", while an already-installed pair not yet used by the origin may still return "downloadable" per spec privacy masking (§6.2).
friction.workaround: Treat "unavailable" as a graceful hide/fallback trigger without assuming a single cause, and always prepare a tap-triggered consent flow for "downloadable".
